chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'I went out to my land, so I shortened (the prayer) for three [days] and completed (the prayer) for three [days].'
ai.seo_question: How many days should a traveler shorten their prayers versus completing them fully?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the duration of the travel period (safar) during which shortening prayers (qasr) is permissible, establishing a ten-day window. It highlights the juristic flexibility (ikhtiyar) granted to the traveler, allowing them to choose between shortening or completing the four-rak'ah prayers on a day-by-day basis within this period. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the temporal scope of the traveler's prayer concession.
